status: Specified before HHAR preprocessing outcomes, model fitting or predictive results
dataset: HHAR smartphone accelerometer only, UCI dataset 344, DOI 10.24432/C5689X
independence: A separately collected cohort not used in the preceding seven-dataset method development or model fits. It is an additional dataset-level confirmation, not proof of independence between every fitted-model statistic.
signals: x,y,z from Phones_accelerometer.csv, all phone device models. No watch, gyroscope or static-still records.
timestamp: Creation_Time in nanoseconds; verify header and timestamp scale before training. Use original per-user/device row order, splitting at non-increasing timestamps, gaps above 0.5 seconds or activity-label changes.
windowing: Within each contiguous run, non-overlapping 5-second windows anchored at the first timestamp. Keep windows with >=60 finite samples, observed duration >=4.9 seconds and maximum gap <=0.5 seconds. Remove incomplete windows and null/unknown activities; do not merge across run boundaries.
resampling: Interpolate each retained window at 200 Hz (1000 points), using endpoint values for the final fractional-sample edge; anti-aliased resample_poly(up=16,down=125,padtype=line) to 128 points. Axes remain unrotated. Standardization is learned on training users only.
resource_cap: At most 1200 retained windows per user, sampled uniformly without replacement without conditioning on class using seed 914271 plus the numeric user ID. This cap is fixed before outcomes and controls repeated-device sample volume and training time. Require all nine users to retain at least 120 windows; otherwise stop and report infeasibility before fitting rather than change the rule after outcomes.
model_definition: Unchanged revision5/models.py: 35-feature LR, MiniRocket with 2016 kernels and LR head, one 6-module InceptionTime-style network trained for 40 epochs. No model selection, new tuning or test-selected checkpoints.
splits: For each seed, uniformly permute the nine users and divide into three test folds of three users. For each fold, independently permute the remaining six users with seed+101*fold; first four train, last two calibrate. All windows and devices of a user share that user's role. Total 5*3*3=45 model cases.
pool_rule: Equal quotas from the two calibration users, sampled without using labels, then uniform random permutation of the complete selected pool.
secondary_score: APS, deterministic inclusive cumulative probabilities with stable class-index ties
primary_comparators: prior/posterior confidence sequence with fixed Beta(9,1) prior
monitoring_batch: All test inputs, with true test labels hidden from acquisition. Return the upper endpoint; use the same monitoring-batch mean set-inflation tolerance for every sequential comparator.
primary_endpoint: Reference-label savings 100*(1-T/N), averaged over paired query draws, models and repetitions within each test user, then equally over the nine users. Primary analysis uses LAC, tolerance 0.5 and N=240.
uncertainty: Report paired differences to both primary comparators with 95-percent participant-bootstrap intervals (10000 resamples; seed 914272), conditional on these fitted models and partitions. Report all nine participant summaries. These are not population-generalization guarantees or independent-configuration tests.
diagnostics: Per-query-run upper-threshold failure, full bracket failure and monitoring-batch inflation exceedance. Also report reference/returned coverage and set size, classifier accuracy and macro-F1, actual pool sizes and retained raw-data counts.
interpretation: Retain zero, negative or statistically uncertain gains. Do not change tolerance, priors, data subset or training duration based on HHAR outcomes. Report HHAR separately from the earlier primary USC-HAD result, with its own protocol date and scope. Do not pool it into an apparently larger preregistered experiment.
human_annotation: No new human labeling-time experiment or self-collected participants. This confirms algorithmic behavior on an additional public cohort only.
